hero.heading: From fragmented process to digital onboarding
hero.subheading1: An onboarding process that lived across forms, WhatsApp, and PDFs.
hero.subheading2: The result was a mobile-only flow — structured, automated, and measurable.
hero.ndaText: Protected by NDA — name changed, real process

role.value: Product Designer — End-to-end redesign of the digital onboarding, from process analysis to mobile-first flow design

vision.value: Turn onboarding into a measurable digital product, aligned with current standards for subscription service onboarding

team.value: Redesign of the operational process, experience architecture, and mobile-first flow. Cross-functional work across teams with legal, technical, and regulatory constraints

metrics.caption: Process reduced from days to minutes

problem.titleLine1: Onboarding didn't live in a system.
problem.body: The process started with a web form, continued on WhatsApp with an advisor, included PDFs to print and sign, validations on external platforms, and manual review by the medical audit team. For the user: opaque, slow, unpredictable. For the organization: total dependency on manual effort, no traceability, no metrics
problem.mensaje: The problem wasn't visual. It was structural

userExperience.title: USER EXPERIENCE
userExperience.body: A long, fragmented journey with no status visibility, unexpected steps, and no clear confirmation

organization.title: ORGANIZATION
organization.body2: Traceability through conversations. Variable timelines. No metrics

timeline: PDF to print, sign, and scan
Manual review by medical audit team

howItEvolved.body: The project was shaped by a strict legal framework, legacy systems, mandatory medical review, and multiple teams with competing priorities. Plus a leadership change mid-process.

phases.label: DISCOVERY
phases.heading: Diagnosis of the original process
phases.body: Mapping of internal states, analysis of validations and friction between teams. Fintech onboarding benchmark. No formal interviews: the starting point was the operational process, not the user
phases.item: Finding: the process follows internal logic, not user logic

phases.label: ITERATION 01 — ORGANIZING COMPLEXITY
phases.heading: Structuring the chaos without changing the model
phases.body: platform with four modules and visible states for the first time: identity, health declaration, payment, signature. The process gained clarity. The model remained intact

phases.label: ITERATION 02 — REDUCING FRICTION
phases.heading: Simplifying within the system
phases.body: A question-by-question review with the legal team. −40% of questions and three documents consolidated into one. A real reduction in cognitive load, not just visual. The flow was still long
phases.item: The problem was still the model

phases.label: THE STRATEGIC SHIFT
phases.heading: With the leadership change, the question changed
phases.body: The goal stopped being to optimize the existing process. It became replacing it.  The user profile already handled complex processes independently. The expected standard was high.
phases.item: Decision: redesign onboarding as a fintech-style mobile-only flow

howItEvolved.closing: The product stopped being a bureaucratic process and became an onboarding

compare.beforeText: How do we optimize the current process?
compare.afterText: Does it make sense for onboarding to keep working like a bureaucratic form?

userExperience.titleLine2: at each stage of the flow.
userExperience.body: The design didn't just solve the structure. It actively changed the user's emotional state at every critical stage.

before.label: 😕 Confused
before.quote: "What do I need to prepare? How long does it take?"

after.label: 🔵 Oriented
after.quote: "I can see the steps. I know how long it'll take. I can start."

before.label: 😰 Anxious
before.quote: "They asked for my info via WhatsApp, my ID photo by message, and sent me to another app for biometrics."

after.label: 🔒 Confident
after.quote: "I scanned my ID, the data filled in automatically, and the validation happened within the same app."

before.label: 😓 Exhausted
before.quote: "There are so many questions. I don't understand why so many."

after.label: 😌 Calm
after.quote: "The questions are few and clear. I'm halfway through."

before.label: 😟 Worried
before.quote: "They didn't tell me anything. Am I still in the process? Did they reject me?"

after.label: ⚡ Invisible
after.quote: "I didn't even notice it. I went straight to the next step."

rows.afterNote: If there are no pre-existing conditions, validation happens in the background. The user doesn't wait.

before.label: 😤 Frustrated
before.quote: "I have to print, sign, and scan. In 2025."

after.label: ✅ Satisfied
after.quote: "I signed and paid in two steps. Done. Easy."

solution.body1: For simple cases, onboarding is completed entirely on mobile. When a validation fails or requires medical judgment, the case is automatically escalated. The advisor stops handling documents and focuses on the cases that actually need them
solution.body2: Onboarding stopped being a sequence of manual tasks and became a system with rules, states, and automated decisions
solution.callout: ⚡ We automated the repetitive and reserved the human touch for what's critical

productDecisions.title: Structural decisions

decisions.title: Mobile-only
decisions.description: Driven by real user behavior. Focusing on one channel forced necessary simplification

decisions.title: Legal simplification
decisions.description: Worked out with the legal team, not imposed. Every reduction required regulatory justification

decisions.title: Selective automation
decisions.description: Low-risk validations automated. Medical exceptions assisted. The goal wasn't to remove humans — it was to redefine when they're needed

decisions.title: Linear and visible flow
decisions.description: In a process involving sensitive data, transparency isn't aesthetic — it's trust
decisions.tradeOff: Trade-off: less flexibility in step order

productDecisions.quoteText: We automated the repetitive. We reserved the human touch for what's critical

metrics.title: Time per stage
metrics.description: Identify where drop-offs happen with real data

metrics.title: Drop-off by step
metrics.description: Detect friction and prioritize with evidence

metrics.title: Real-time states
metrics.description: Full visibility for the operations team

designSystem.body1: The visual system was designed to convey clarity and trust within a sensitive process
designSystem.body2: Red was avoided as a dominant color in critical moments to prevent premature associations with rejection or failure
designSystem.body3: Instead, we used a neutral color scale with emphasis on informational states and explicit messaging, prioritizing textual clarity over implicit emotional signals. Alerts were handled with moderate tones and specific copy, ensuring clear feedback without adding unnecessary friction

items.title: The problem wasn't the UI. It was the model
items.description: Improving the interface of a broken process doesn't make it less broken. The real progress came when the whole model was questioned, not when the existing flow was optimized

items.title: Organizing wasn't simplifying
items.description: Giving visual shape to complexity doesn't reduce complexity. The first iteration confirmed it: the process had a new form, but it was still the same process

items.title: Digitizing wasn't enough
items.description: Moving a physical process to a screen doesn't make it a digital product. The operational model needed to change, not just the channel

items.title: The impact was in the system, not the screens
items.description: Turning a scattered process into a measurable product — with metrics, the ability to evolve, and clear ownership over every part of the flow

takeaways.quote: When the problem is structural, design has to go further than the interface

methodology.heading: I turn complex processes into digital products
methodology.paragraph: I design as a decision system, not a screen production line. Before opening Figma, I define the problem, the flows, and the decisions that actually impact the business.

steps.title: Map

steps.title: Flows

steps.title: Wireframes

steps.title: Launch

principles.heading: Non-negotiable principles
principles.body: My work follows a set of rules that ensure the final result is not just beautiful, but functional and scalable.
principles.whereBody: I work best with teams that value data-driven design, technical transparency, and fast iteration. My ideal environment is one where design has a seat at the strategy table.
principles.wontFindIntro: My process is rigorous. For results to be high-impact, there are certain practices I've chosen to leave out of my workflow.
wontFindItems: Decorative design: If an element doesn't have a clear function, it doesn't exist in my interface.
Creative ego: I prioritize business goals and usability over my personal aesthetic preferences.
Lack of documentation: I don't deliver messy files. Every component is named and documented for engineering.

cards.title: Diagnosis
cards.description: I don't start designing without understanding the "why." Every pixel responds to a previously diagnosed need.

cards.title: Decisions
cards.description: Every design decision is grounded. I don't use trends for the sake of it, but for their communicative effectiveness.

cards.title: Focus
cards.description: I cut the noise. Good design is what allows the user to complete their task with the least mental effort possible.

cards.title: Cycles
cards.description: Design is never "done." I work in continuous improvement cycles based on feedback and metrics.

cards.title: Components
cards.description: I design for the future. I build atomic component libraries that allow products to scale without losing visual consistency.

contactCTA.heading: Let's talk.
contactCTA.paragraph: I work best with founders or product teams at an early or growth stage, with a concrete operational problem that design can solve. If you're looking for just pretty screens, I'm probably not the right fit.
contactCTA.typicalProjects: Typical projects: digital onboarding · B2B platforms · operational process redesign · systems with technical or legal constraints.
